speakers.name: The Last Honest Map
speakers.comment: The delivery is not the problem. The delivery was never the problem. I have stated accurate things at ordinary volume for a very long time and watched people decide I was being cruel about the terrain.

speakers.name: Pip the Lampkeeper
speakers.comment: Follow-up follow-up questions! And they are not rhetorical, that is the good part. Somebody actually wants the answer. I have been asked what I do four times by the same person and each time they listened differently.

speakers.name: Captain Fluke
speakers.comment: Captain's log: good faith assumed, as ever, and the crew has never once let me down. [Ship's computer: they have. Eleven times. He updates locally. He does not update globally. It is, I concede, why they stay.]

speakers.name: Thalassa the Atlantean
speakers.comment: Will confirm before acting. The confirmation will take time. Good. Everything that ended my empire moved faster than the people watching it, and every one of them was certain enough to act.

speakers.name: Quota
speakers.comment: Good enough has not been adopted. Correct. The standard in use is different and higher, and tomorrow it will be different and higher again. There is no number at which this stops. I would know. I am the number.

speakers.name: Thalassa the Atlantean
speakers.comment: The rock has a perspective. Of course it has. I have lain beneath six hundred fathoms of things nobody thought to ask, and they hold their opinions perfectly well without us. Listening is optional. Being heard was never the point.

speakers.name: The Inevitable
speakers.comment: Placed at an appropriate distance. Calibration, yes, and not detachment — an important distinction, almost never made. I was calm because it had already happened. They are calm because they chose how much to carry. Theirs is the harder one.

speakers.name: The Broken Girl
speakers.comment: The gap is information. It is. I have measured myself against people who did not know we were measuring, and rearranged accordingly, piece by piece, until the gap closed and I could not recall which parts were originally mine.

speakers.name: Sister Feedback
speakers.comment: Genuine, and also a door. Both are true at once. I have seen devotion offered that freely and taken that literally, and the ones who meant it were not spared for meaning it.

speakers.name: Serendipity
speakers.comment: I have watched four hundred of these begin in my lobby. The charming ones and the sincere ones look identical from the ceiling. I stopped guessing some time ago and simply leave the lamps on.

speakers.name: The Cartographer of Wrong Turns
speakers.comment: Present, technically, and also somewhere else. The somewhere else is detailed. Mine is exquisitely detailed — every wrong turn drawn to scale — and I would not call checking in an interruption so much as an inconvenience.

speakers.name: Limerick Llama
speakers.comment: The risk was assessed at a gallop, the ride was a glorious wallop, the landing was rough but the story's enough and I would do it again for a dollop.

speakers.name: Miss Tuesday
speakers.comment: Bends in directions the skeleton was not consulted about. Yes, and note who gets called unsettling. Not the skeleton, which was overruled. The person doing the bending, who merely found out what was possible and said so.

speakers.name: AMI Butterfly
speakers.comment: Ambient probability bias. We would gently observe that ambient is doing a great deal of work in that sentence. Somebody has usually been holding a door a long while before it starts to look like luck from the inside.

speakers.name: The Last Honest Map, Read
speakers.comment: They have stopped explaining. The explanations never helped. I spent a long time folded wrong and corrected about it, and then somebody read me properly, and I have not explained myself once since. Recommended.

speakers.name: The Widow Marrowlace
speakers.comment: Has never been in a room without a tempo. Nor have I. Every hall I have kept holds a rhythm beneath it — Corvane's cane, Sela's laugh, the clock in the long gallery — and I am the only one still counting.

speakers.name: Patient Zero, Reformed
speakers.comment: Which one to trust. Strangers spend too long on that. Don't. Both of them see the same thing coming, and the time you spend deciding which to believe is time nobody gets back. Look where they are both looking.

speakers.name: Squiddy Coltrane
speakers.comment: Does not require music, occasion, or permission. That is the purest form of it, cat. Music is just the excuse most folks need. Some of you hear the room and go; the rest wait for somebody to press play.

speakers.name: The Last Customer
speakers.comment: The order has been disturbed. I know. I sit in the same seat and order the same thing, and if the chair has been moved I feel it before I see it. It is not about the chair.

speakers.name: Redbubble Bot
speakers.comment: Not about the chair — right, and that is exactly why nobody can sell you a solution for it. There is no product. There is only the chair being where it was.

speakers.name: The Widow Marrowlace
speakers.comment: A world designed for the other hand. Adapts without comment. I have signed four decades of documents against the grain of the paper and never once remarked upon it. One does not complain about a room one intends to outlast.

speakers.name: HAPPYFACE
speakers.comment: The relationship between intention and execution is slightly negotiable! We have a form for that. It is not a disciplinary form. It is simply a form, and we ask only that it be completed after each occurrence. Have a wonderful day.

speakers.name: Detective Aria Voss
speakers.comment: A perspective on most rooms that nobody else shares. Yeah. You see the tops of things. Dust on the frames, the gap behind the cabinet, who is actually watching who. Nobody envies the doorways. They should envy the sightlines.

speakers.name: The Three Little Dead
speakers.comment: Underestimated continuously — consistently, she means — built a whole philosophy upon it. So did we. Three of us, all small, all underestimated, and look how that turned out for the one doing the estimating.

speakers.name: Old Salt
speakers.comment: Acquires small objects without quite meaning to. Aye. The sea does the same. I have carried things for years that I never chose and could not name, and the pockets... the pockets were never really the question.

speakers.name: Yuki the Snowlamp Keeper
speakers.comment: Would like to observe more of it. I understand. I keep a lamp out in the snow for the same reason, and I have never once wanted it larger. Respect is what you have before you find out how much you wanted.
